messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: RRPP v 1.1.0 released on CRAN
parts:
Dear Colleagues,

I wish to alert you to some updates to the RRPP R package, the linear model workhorse for the geomorph package.  Version 1.1.0 is now available on CRAN and Github (mlcollyer/RRPP), and for the moment, both versions are the same.  This is a minor release.  Although most releases are patch releases — fix bugs or modify functions — this minor release largely updates all support code to be compliant with R 4.1 updates, and is, therefore, more comprehensive, even if no changes are apparent.  I urge you to update this package, even if geomorph appears to be working fine.  One of the issues we encountered is dropped data names, especially for data that could be coerced into either a vector or matrix, which renders indexing either impossible, or worse, erroneous (in which case a result could be produced that shouldn’t be produced).  Updates should not affect geomorph functions, but it is possible that our battery of tests missed an issue.  If you find an issue, please alert me.  With large-scale coding changes, additional patch updates might be needed.

In spite of the R 4.1 update spurring the RRPP 1.1.0 release, we also have a new function (tool) for a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure (looCV), which can be used on lm.rrpp, procD.lm, or procD.pgls linear model fits.  This function is based on the procedure described by Cardini and Polly (2020) and should be similar to the tools just published by Thioulouse and colleagues in the ade4 package, which work in conjunction with other analytical tools there.  These papers address more specifically the spurious between-group graphical differences that might manifest from between-groups PCA (bgPCA) of high-dimensional data, even in spite of no true group differences, as pointed out by Cardini et al. (2019).  Our function is a little different in that it can be used with any linear model (including one that use GLS estimation) where PCA is performed on the fitted values from the model.  This function is most effective when used with its S3 plotting associated function, plot.looCV, which plots side-by-side the PC plot of a fitted model — the same as plot(fit, type = “PC”, …) — and the plot of cross-validated scores.  (If they are similar, it supports the real differences between groups; if they are different, it supports the conclusion that apparent group differences are spurious in the low-dimensional projection.)

The RRPP::looCV function has a couple of differences compared to the tools in the ade4 package, which are explained in the associated help file.  This function should work well in the RRPP/geomorph environment, without having to reformat results from lm.rrpp/procD.lm/procD.pgls objects (which also means it can be used with PGLS analyses).

With warm regards!

Mike (on behalf of Mike and Dean)
